title: fix: handle upstream Cloudflare timeouts
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Maps upstream Cloudflare 524 responses to the standard 502 error envelope
- Tries declared model fallbacks after an upstream 524
- Keeps the existing 300-second durable-generation contract
- Covers status mapping, fallback selection, and the community image fallback route

Fixes #14300

gist.headline: Timeouts Find Another Flower
gist.blurb: When an upstream Cloudflare 524 lingers too long, the hive now sends the request toward its declared fallback models. The 300-second durable-generation promise remains intact; the error handling just grew better hiking boots.
gist.summary: Cloudflare upstream 524 timeouts are now normalized into the standard 502 error envelope, and image requests try their declared model fallbacks while preserving the existing 300-second durable-generation contract.
gist.impact: When an upstream image provider times out, users get consistent 502 responses and eligible requests can continue through configured fallback models instead of ending at the first stalled route.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy garden path where a stalled Cloudflare-shaped rain cloud blocks one route to a glowing image-generation greenhouse, while Polli follows a clearly marked alternate path to a healthy fallback flower. A small CRT monitor robot can hold a pixel sign reading "502 → FALLBACK," making the status normalization and automatic rerouting legible; include code-plants and a 300-second sand timer to represent the preserved durable-generation window.
